messages:
yuki: noticed a spike of tiny-pod pendings in eu-west1 this morning, seems correlated with warm-node handoffs from the warmpool. pods sit Pending ~45s then either get preempted or evicted. anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw it too. traces show node becomes Ready but the prebind label mutation arrives later, pods time out on prebind path.

eng-scheduler-bot: alert: 6 pending pods >30s on node warmpool-handovers-eu-west1c (metric: scheduler.prebind.latency)

olga: can you paste the logs? is this the prebind webhook or some daemon that applies gpu labels?

yuki: minimal logs:
```
I0321 07:12:03 scheduler.go:243] PreBind start pod/mini-train-abc
I0321 07:12:03 node-watcher: observed node warmpool-xyz NotReady->Ready
I0321 07:12:47 prebind-webhook: label-apply latency 36s for node warmpool-xyz
I0321 07:12:48 scheduler.go:285] PreBind failed: node labels missing
```

raj: that 36s label apply is the kicker. our warmpool handoff script waits for kubelet Ready then assumes labels are present. looks like a race with node-label-sync daemon.

oncall: happening across a couple racks, but concentrated in one AZ, so might be ordering in our node init hooks after image boot.

sam: workaround idea: bump prebind timeout in scheduler config from 30s -> 90s for tiny jobs class, and add a short requeue backoff so pods don't immediately evict. cheap experiment.

olga: alternatively we could make the node init path idempotent: ensure label daemon updates labels before Ready. which is easier short-term?

yuki: short-term: config tweak + metric checkpoint to avoid customer impact. long-term: fix init ordering. I'll open a canary rollout.

sam: config snippet to test (scheduler-configmap):
```
policy:
  podClasses:
    tiny:
      prebindTimeoutSeconds: 90
      requeueDelaySeconds: 8
```

raj: also adding a probe in node-init to push labels earlier would reduce tail latency. e.g., run label-sync before marking node Ready or delay Ready until label-propagation completes.

olga: beware of delaying node Ready too long — that blocks autoscaler accounting. maybe mark internal-ready and let controller flip actual Ready after labels? messy.

oncall: after switching tiny prebind to 90s on canary, pending >30s dropped by ~85% for the test group. no significant increase in overall scheduling latency observed. :thumbsup:

yuki: I'll roll the config to 5% first, monitor scheduler.prebind.latency and pending_count per-podclass. also creating an incident ticket for the init ordering fix.

sam: created PR with config change + metrics dashboard link: https://go/redux/dashboards/warmpool-prebind?env=eu-west1

raj: longterm checklist for this issue: [1] make label-sync idempotent and run before Ready, [2] add a fast label cache lookup in scheduler prebind, [3] add retry path to prebind binding that waits for label arrival for tiny pods.

olga: FYI cost note — these pending tiny pods trigger node churn and short-lived evictions which spike our migration egress a bit. avoid too long timeouts.

yuki: noted. will watch egress and eviction_rate. tagging @oncall for followups.

oncall: ack, will keep an eye for the next 2h and escalate if pending_count climbs back.

sam: thanks all — followup in #eng-platform once canary results stable.
